open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct, or refute by a specific encoded experiment, a finite shared-trace recession library satisfying canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate, simultaneous-collar compatibility, translated-uniform tails, and an input-computable refinement schedule with vanishing accumulated error.
open_obligations.obstruction: The available active-set geometry controls only forward motion from a fixed mean. It does not preserve every active semantic region \(D_v\) and the separated-risk set \(H_r\) on canonical sections throughout protected stars. Face-vertex equality does not bound actual face--cone differences over collar overlap, and neither translated-uniform tail control nor a refinement-count recurrence is available.
open_obligations.attempted: The prior construction used one smoothed ancestor, one common rational simplicial fan, literally shared raywise Foelner factors, and shared finite-element face variables. These yield path-independent operators and translation-boundary ratios, but the proposed collar induction becomes circular if it defines traces from the glued rule and may be unsafe under constant extension. No further generic averaging argument closes the branching-incidence estimates.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Starting from the single ancestor \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\), \(\mathrm{lem:common\mbox{-}ray\mbox{-}folner\mbox{-}coherence}\) proves that, for every face inclusion \(\tau\preceq\sigma\),
\[
q_{\sigma,L}
=
\left(
\prod_{\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)\setminus\mathscr R(\tau)}
\mathsf A_{\varrho,L}
\right)q_{\tau,L},
\]
independently of the incidence path, together with the bounds
\[
\left\|q_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-q_{\sigma,L}(w)\right\|_1
\leq 2\min\{1,a/L\}
\]
and
\[
\left|F^f_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-F^f_{\sigma,L}(w)\right|
\leq R_f\min\{1,a/L\}.
\]
The smoothing, one-chart averaging, and weighted path results separately give
\[
R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\},
\qquad
\frac{R_fk}{T\sqrt{2\pi}},
\qquad
\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f+\frac{R_f}{2}\omega(h)
\]
for each fixed finite library. The simultaneous collar-safety, translated-tail, and growing-refinement estimates required for effective compatible density remain unproved.

prose_updates.tldr: The unconditional contribution consists of three proved pieces: common-ray Foelner operators are path-independent and have explicit translation-boundary ratios; Carter’s bounded-ratio kernels give fixed-base compact multinomial transfer with separately displayed semantic, covariance, and \(C_{2/\kappa}m\log(m)/\sqrt n\) charges; and compact exhaustion gives a global minimax lower limit together with two-sided convergence on diagonally selected expanding lawful windows, but no global upper limit. Replayable moving-offset transfer and CertGluePFL termination remain conditional on an affirmative resolution of the effective-compatible-density question or on a separately proved sufficient compatibility package.

project_justification.gap: Carter’s bounded-ratio comparison controls fixed-base compact multinomial experiments after separate semantic and covariance charges, but it does not construct a finite Gaussian recession library or make moving-offset replayability automatic. At infinity, common-ray commutativity does not control all incident rules mixed on simultaneous collars. The unresolved question is whether the encoded rational geometry admits canonical-section safety, positive-weight candidate safety, translated-uniform tails, and a computable refinement schedule whose total ledger vanishes.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification inference combines discontinuous completed labels, intersecting unbounded recession faces, and a global honesty constraint. Equality on a geometric face does not control all candidates mixed on nearby simultaneous collars, while compact local asymptotics cannot detect a hard seam escaping to infinity. The proved compact/windowed theory and the unanswered compatibility-density question at unbounded recession seams are therefore mathematically distinct.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves common-ray operator coherence, Carter-based fixed-base compact transfer with separate semantic and covariance terms, a global minimax lower limit, and two-sided convergence on diagonally selected expanding lawful windows. It does not prove global effective compatible density. The corresponding open-ended question lists the five certificates still required. Replayable moving-offset rules and CertGluePFL termination are asserted only under an affirmative answer or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On every fixed compact, base convergence and the centered local expansion imply eventual positive cells and lawful causal parameters. Carter contributes only the bounded-ratio experiment error; score means, covariance replacement, active-face remainders, rational offsets, and semantic-union displacement are charged separately. Compact convergence permits a diagonal choice of expanding lawful windows after the relevant compact moduli vanish, but it supplies no algorithm for computing the semantic displacement, lawful-ball inclusion, covariance error, or required suprema. Moving-offset comparison is therefore qualitative unless effective rational upper enclosures for those quantities are separately supplied.

prose_updates.related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) supplies the bounded-ratio comparison between a fixed positive-cell multinomial experiment and its matched multivariate normal experiment through parameter-independent kernels. The present work separately charges score-map, covariance-replacement, completed-affine-arrangement, and moving-offset errors and uses diagonally selected lawful windows for compact exhaustion. Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes (2013, Assumptions A--B and Proposition 1) study randomized treatment with monotone employment and the always-employed comparison. Their model embeds in the present causal class only on the singleton-\(X\) submodel with known rational assignment probabilities \(\bar\pi_z\geq\pi_*\), perfect compliance \(D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=z\), \(s=+1\), both potential wages on the finite grid \(\mathcal Y\), and \(P(\mathrm{EE})\geq m_*>0\). On that submodel every unit is a complier, \(\mathrm{ASC}=\mathrm{EE}\), and \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(\mathrm{EE})\); there is no unrestricted-class inclusion or automatic sharpness transfer. Day and Markov--Kakutani invariant-mean theory and Namioka’s 1964 Foelner conditions concern a single amenable commuting action and provide neither an input-computable modulus nor semantic coverage, separated-risk safety, translated-tail control, or branching-refinement complexity.
prose_updates.interpretation: The Gaussian experiment is the valid local decision target on each fixed lawful direction window. Carter’s bounded-ratio kernels yield an unconditional qualitative compact comparison for any supplied Gaussian rule after the semantic and covariance charges are added. A finite replayable moving-offset rule is conditional on an affirmative effective-compatible-density conclusion, or on a separately proved sufficient compatibility package, and its replayable numerical accounting additionally requires separately supplied effective rational upper envelopes for the semantic displacement and covariance-replacement errors. Compact exhaustion gives a global minimax lower limit and two-sided convergence only along diagonally selected expanding lawful windows; it gives neither a global upper limit nor an algorithm for selecting those windows. The common-ray library is an algebraically coherent recession representation, not a compatibility-density theorem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Effective compatible density is unresolved under the standing assumptions. One unproved obligation is to show that every canonical chart section remains in each required \(D_v\), \(H_r\), and declared chart-neighborhood incidence region. The remaining obligations are safety of every positive-weight candidate; exact overlap traces or a valid Gaussian-weighted face-cone discrepancy bound on simultaneous supports; translated-uniform guard and normal-base tails; and computed refinement counts \(N_j\) with schedules \(L_j,B_j,\delta_j\) for which every accumulated error vanishes and \(N_j/L_j\) tends to zero. No refinement-independent ledger constant is assumed. The four-label milliscale certificate and unconditional global CertGluePFL termination therefore remain unresolved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target is the same-law joint identified set and is only contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp endpoint intervals; no Cartesian joint sharpness is claimed. Carter-backed sampled-data conclusions are fixed-compact or expanding-window statements. Compact exhaustion proves a global lower limit and two-sided windowed convergence, but neither a global \(\limsup\) nor a globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal. The paper proves common-ray operator identities, Gaussian smoothing, one-chart averaging, and the weighted telescoping inequality for any already specified finite family with certified edge discrepancies. It does not prove existence of finite families whose total compatibility ledger vanishes. Effective compatible density remains an open-ended question, and CertGluePFL termination and replayable global Gaussian certification remain conditional.

statement_notes.justification: This question isolates the exact effective geometric package still needed to turn coherent recession operators into a finite globally honest search space.
statement_notes.gap: The standing assumptions do not yet yield simultaneous canonical-section safety, collar compatibility, translated-uniform tails, or a refinement schedule whose total ledger vanishes.
statement_notes.consumer: Only an affirmative answer, or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package, can supply the displayed premise of the conditional CertGluePFL termination theorem.

proofs.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: parameter-independent Le Cam transfer, an explicit Gaussian Hellinger calculation, and finite-arrangement stability.}

Write \(D_n=\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}\), \(I_n=B'D_n^{-1}B\), and \(\Sigma_n=I_n^{-1}\).  By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), uniformly over \(u\in C\), all multinomial coordinates are eventually at least \(\kappa/2\), their largest-to-smallest ratio is at most \(2/\kappa\), and Carter's parameter-independent kernel has total-variation error
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}
=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
For a matched normal vector \(Y_n\), apply the parameter-independent affine score map
\[
S_n(Y_n)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\frac{Y_n-np_n(0)}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Its law at \(p_n(u)\) is \(N_d\{\mu_n(u),V_n(u)\}\), where
\[
\mu_n(u)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\},                         \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
V_n(u)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}
\left[\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(u)\}-p_n(u)p_n(u)'\right]
D_n^{-1}B\Sigma_n.                                                            \tag{3}
\]
Because \(\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}B=I_d\), (2) gives
\[
\sup_{u\in C}\|\mu_n(u)-u\|_2
\leq \|\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}d_n(C)\longrightarrow0.           \tag{4}
\]
The last convergence uses \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\), while eventual boundedness of the matrix norm follows from \(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\), \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), the full column rank of \(B\), and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\).  Equations (3)--(4), the same lemma, and compactness of \(C\) imply
\[
\sup_{u\in C}\|V_n(u)-\Sigma_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0.            \tag{5}
\]

For positive definite \(V\), direct completion of squares in the integral of the square root of the two Gaussian densities gives
\[
\mathsf H^2(\mu,V;u,\Sigma_0)
=2-2\frac{|V|^{1/4}|\Sigma_0|^{1/4}}
{|(V+\Sigma_0)/2|^{1/2}}
\exp\left[-\frac18(\mu-u)'\{(V+\Sigma_0)/2\}^{-1}(\mu-u)\right].          \tag{6}
\]
The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied to the positive and negative parts of the density difference yields total variation at most \(\min\{1,\mathsf H\}\).  Define
\[
\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
=\sup_{u\in C}\min\{1,\mathsf H(\mu_n(u),V_n(u);u,\Sigma_0)\}.              \tag{7}
\]
Uniform positive definiteness following from (5), together with (4)--(6), proves
\[
\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\longrightarrow0.                            \tag{8}
\]

The exact moving-slack identity in \(\text{def:moving-slack-system}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) give a finite active-set constant \(H_C\) such that every finite-sample semantic label at \(u\in C\) is an incident Gaussian label at a point displaced by at most \(H_Cx_n(C)\) in \(\Sigma_0^{-1}\)-norm.  The same enumeration applies to each rival semantic union and to each active projection system defining the separated domain; enlarging \(H_C\) by the maximum of the finitely many inverse-basis norms charges the corresponding risk-set restoration.  Equalities lose no label because every equality face belongs to all incident completions.  Translation of equal-covariance Gaussian laws by Mahalanobis distance \(t\) has total variation \(2\Phi(t/2)-1\leq t/\sqrt{2\pi}\), so its numerical factor may also be absorbed into this finite \(H_C\).

Set the protected-band width equal to \(\tau=x_n(C)\).  The indicator \(\mathbf1\{x_n(C)>\tau\}\) is then zero.  Since every \(a_j\ne0\) and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), each denominator below is positive, and the definition of \(\mathfrak b_0\) gives, for every \(x\geq0\),
\[
\mathfrak b_0(x)
=\sum_j\min\left\{1,
\frac{2x}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}\right\}
\leq A_0x.                                                                     \tag{9}
\]
Thus the complete semantic contribution is at most
\[
H_Cx_n(C)+\mathfrak b_0\{x_n(C)\}
\leq(H_C+A_0)x_n(C).                                                           \tag{10}
\]
Finally, apply \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\) to the Carter kernel, to the score-normal covariance replacement, and to the Gaussian translations used in (10).  Coverage indicators take values in \([0,1]\), and \(0\leq\ell_0\leq1\), so (1), (7), and (10) add without a loss-scale multiplier and yield exactly \(\widetilde{\mathcal E}_n(C)\).  The convergence \(d_n(C)\to0\) is \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\), the convergence \(\delta_n(C)\to0\) is \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\), and (8) handles covariance replacement.  Hence \(\widetilde{\mathcal E}_n(C)\to0\).  Because neither cited premise supplies a rate for the last three quantities, no overall \(O(n^{-1/2})\) assertion follows.

\textbf{Technique: unconditional comparison followed by a separately conditional construction step.}

For every active cut, (12) and \(\text{ass:local-family-affine-hull}\) imply \(c_n\in\mathcal K_0\).  The effective offset-encoding assumption therefore returns the stated rational \(\widehat c_n\) for each chosen rational \(\xi_n>0\).  The local expansion assumption and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) imply
\[
d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\longrightarrow0.                                    \tag{18}
\]
Taking \(\overline\chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\) proves existence of a vanishing upper bound, but makes no claim that this particular real number is computably available.  Applying \(\text{lem:moving-offset-carter-geometry}\) to any supplied Gaussian rule gives exactly \(\Delta_n(C)\); (18) and covariance convergence imply \(\Delta_n(C)\to0\).  This proves the unconditional qualitative statistical comparison.

We also check that the rational offset experiment used below is legal.  Since \(\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\) and all defining matrices are rational, exact row reduction returns a rational \(z_n\in\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\) such that \(A_\Psi z_n=\widehat c_n\).  For every fixed \(u\), relative interiority and tangent-image compatibility, applied to \(z_n+Bu\), give a sufficiently small \(t>0\) with
\[
p_0+t(z_n+Bu)\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}.                                    \tag{18a}
\]
The active signs of this lawful lift are exactly the signs of \(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u\), with zero assigned to every incident completion.  Thus \(\text{prop:tangent-fan-global-cover}\) and its completed-lift argument give a full semantic cover for the offset cells.  A strict chamber of the common homogeneous arrangement remains strict after adding the fixed offset: along a sufficiently long multiple \(ty\), every rival component has a violated nonzero row with gap \(t\gamma+O(1)\), \(\gamma>0\).  For every point \(g\) of that component,
\[
t\gamma+O(1)\leq a'(ty-g)
\leq\|a\|_{\Sigma_0}\|ty-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}.                              \tag{18b}
\]
The positive definiteness of \(\Sigma_0\) makes \(\|a\|_{\Sigma_0}>0\).  Taking the infimum over \(g\), and then the minimum over finitely many rivals, proves nonemptiness of the offset separated domain for the fixed \(r_0\).  If there is no active cut, there is one global semantic label and the conclusion is immediate.  Hence the rational offset object belongs to \(\mathfrak E\).

Now impose, only for the constructive conclusion, the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\), or a separately proved package supplying the same finite Gaussian approximation certificates.  The conditional \(\text{thm:certglue-termination}\) then produces a rational finite rule for \(\mathfrak G_0(\widehat c_n)\), an outward Gaussian ledger \(\rho_{\mathrm{led},n}\), and a finite atomic dual.  If effective rational upper enclosures for the three comparison quantities named in the statement are also supplied, choose the collar width
\[
\tau_n=\overline\chi_n(C),                                                     \tag{19}
\]
not a square-root schedule.  Equations (15)--(16) show that the moving-face charge is at most \(2A_0\overline\chi_n(C)\).  Dovetail the finite Gaussian-certificate accuracy, truncation, integration, and rounding searches so that
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{led},n}+\operatorname{Tail}_n(C)+\operatorname{Round}_n
\longrightarrow0.                                                             \tag{20}
\]
The full outward bound is consequently
\[
\Delta_n(C)+\rho_{\mathrm{led},n}
+\operatorname{Tail}_n(C)+\operatorname{Round}_n.                             \tag{21}
\]
If the unrepaired finite Gaussian rule has coverage deficit \(\rho_n<1\), \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\) mixes in \(V\) with probability \(\rho_n/(\eta_0+\rho_n)\).  The denominator is positive because \(\eta_0>0\), the repaired coverage is exactly at least \(1-\eta_0\), and the normalized risk increases by at most \(\rho_n/(\eta_0+\rho_n)\).  All quantities in (19)--(21) then have supplied rational outward enclosures, so this conditional construction is replayable.  Without those additional statistical envelopes, (18) still proves qualitative convergence but not an algorithmic stopping index.  Every infimum and supremum in this argument is restricted to \(C\), which proves the final non-global clause.

\textbf{Technique: diagonal compact exhaustion, finite-support dual transfer, and exact windowwise repair.}

Let \(B_k=\{u:\|u\|_2\leq k\}\), and fix \(k\).  By \(\text{lem:compact-causal-domain}\), the relative-interior, affine-hull, base-convergence, and compact local-expansion premises give
\[
B_k\subseteq\mathcal U_n                                                               \tag{22}
\]
eventually.  By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), also
\[
\min_{u\in B_k}\min_{j\in\mathcal J}p_{n,j}(u)\geq\kappa/2                           \tag{23}
\]
eventually.  Zero-offset centering, the local expansion, and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) make every term in \(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\) tend to zero for each fixed \(\ell\).  Since there are only finitely many \(1\leq\ell\leq k\), (22)--(23) and \(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\leq1/\ell\) hold simultaneously for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Hence the maximum defining \(R_n^\diamond\) is eventually at least \(k\).  Since \(k\) was arbitrary,
\[
R_n^\diamond\longrightarrow\infty.                                                \tag{24}
\]
This is an existence argument based on convergence indices; it does not compute those indices.  At the selected radius, the defining diagonal inequalities and \(R_n^\diamond\to\infty\) give a deterministic total comparison deficit \(\rho_n\to0\).

Fix \(L<M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  By \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), a finite atomic Gaussian dual \(\mu\) has value greater than \(L\).  Its finitely many coverage and risk support points lie in some \(B_k\).  By zero-offset centering and \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\), each coverage atom in \(D_v^0\) has a realization in \(D_{n,v}\cap B_{k+1}\) at Mahalanobis distance tending to zero.  A separate realization is used for every incident constraint role, so equality faces retain all required labels.

For a risk atom, the directed rival-union bounds in the same finite enumeration preserve membership in \(H_{n,r_0}\) after an arbitrarily small active-set correction.  When \(r_0>0\), the zero-offset cells are cones and positive homogeneity permits replacing an atom \(h\) by \((1+t_n)h\), with \(t_n\downarrow0\), so that its separation margin dominates twice the arrangement error.  When \(r_0=0\), uniqueness of the atom's label and closedness of the finite rival union give positive atom-specific distance; an incident open-chamber approximation handles equality atoms.  The finite number of atoms makes all corrections simultaneous.  By (24), their realizations lie in \(B_{R_n^\diamond}\) eventually.

Apply Carter's reverse parameter-independent kernel to an arbitrary window-honest multinomial rule, followed by the score and covariance maps.  By \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\), the change in the finite dual objective is at most \(A_\mu\rho_n\), where \(A_\mu<\infty\) is the sum of the absolute dual coefficients.  Weak duality gives
\[
M_n^\diamond\geq L-A_\mu\rho_n.                                               \tag{25}
\]
First let \(n\to\infty\), and then let \(L\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\), to obtain
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n^\diamond
\geq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).                                          \tag{26}
\]

For the reverse inequality, fix \(a>0\).  The attainment part of \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\) supplies a measurable \(K^a\in\mathcal C_{\eta_0}\) with
\[
\sup_{h\in H_{r_0}}E_h\ell_0\{K^a(W_0)\}
\leq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a.                                        \tag{27}
\]
No finite representation is needed for this unconditional argument.  Transfer \(K^a\) by the forward Carter kernel on \(B_{R_n^\diamond}\).  The exact slack identity, finite completed-arrangement comparison, covariance replacement, and the inequalities accepted in the diagonal definition give window coverage at least \(1-\eta_0-\rho_n\) and risk at most
\[
M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n.                                      \tag{28}
\]
The same radial correction for \(r_0>0\), and the finite open-chamber correction for \(r_0=0\), are among the finite-arrangement charges in \(\mathscr E_n(R_n^\diamond)\); thus (28) uses the exact separated set, not an \(r_0-o(1)\) substitute.

Apply the algebra of \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\) with coverage infima restricted to the window.  With
\[
q_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n},
\]
the denominator is positive and
\[
(1-q_n)(1-\eta_0-\rho_n)+q_n=1-\eta_0.                                      \tag{29}
\]
Since \(0\leq\ell_0\leq1\), (28)--(29) imply
\[
M_n^\diamond\leq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n
+\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.                                               \tag{30}
\]
Letting \(n\to\infty\), then \(a\downarrow0\), and combining (26) and (30) proves
\[
M_n^\diamond\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).                  \tag{31}
\]
The global feasible class is contained in the window-feasible class, while the global risk supremum is over a superset of the window risk domain.  Therefore \(M_n\geq M_n^\diamond\), and (31) yields
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n\geq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).                 \tag{32}
\]

If the effective-compatible-density question is affirmatively resolved, the conditional \(\text{thm:certglue-termination}\) supplies finite Gaussian upper rules.  The additional rational envelopes named in \(\text{thm:moving-offset-transfer}\), if supplied, make their sampled-data transfer and repair replayable; neither ingredient was used in (22)--(32).  Finally, \(\text{lem:escaping-boundary-kill}\) gives two arrays identical on every fixed compact but with different global upper behavior.  It rules out any global \(\limsup\) conclusion from the premises used here.

\textbf{Technique: effective dovetailing of sound primal and dual semidecisions under the displayed conditional premise.}

Fix \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\).  The conditional premise supplies a computable \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)\downarrow0\) such that, for each \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\), finite records \(Q_j(K)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) are eventually enumerated and certify
\[
\begin{split}
c\{Q_j(K)\}&\geq1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
r\{Q_j(K)\}&\leq R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
\rho_{\mathrm{led}}\{Q_j(K)\}&\leq\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),
\end{split}                                                                    \tag{33}
\]
where \(c(Q)\) is the infimum of semantic-label coverage and \(r(Q)\) is the separated diameter risk.  The premise also supplies the finite canonical-section, positive-weight safety, collar-discrepancy, translated-tail, and refinement-count receipts needed to verify (33); none is inferred from amenability.

At stage \(s\), enumerate all \(j\leq s\), all records in \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) of code length at most \(s\), all associated exact rational incidence forests and semantic projections, and the first \(s\) rational integration and rounding precisions.  The ledger checks return outward rational enclosures
\[
c^-_{Q,s}\leq c(Q),\qquad r(Q)\leq r^+_{Q,s}.                                 \tag{34}
\]
Acceptance requires every polyhedral incidence, protected-neighborhood, Gaussian-tail, covariance, quadrature, and rounding check supporting (34).  Define
\[
\rho_{Q,s}=\max\{0,1-\eta-c^-_{Q,s}\},
\qquad q_{Q,s}=\frac{\rho_{Q,s}}{\eta+\rho_{Q,s}}.                            \tag{35}
\]
After intersecting the coverage enclosure with \([0,1]\),
\[
0\leq\rho_{Q,s}\leq1-\eta<1,
\qquad \eta+\rho_{Q,s}>0,                                                       \tag{36}
\]
so the division is valid.  From (34)--(35), \(c(Q)\geq1-\eta-\rho_{Q,s}\).  By \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\), the archived rule \(Q^+=\operatorname{Repair}_{\eta,\rho_{Q,s}}(Q)\) is globally honest and
\[
M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
\leq R_r(Q^+)
\leq r^+_{Q,s}+Dq_{Q,s}.                                                        \tag{37}
\]
Outward interval arithmetic supplies a rational \(U_{Q,s}\) no smaller than the last expression.

In parallel, enumerate the finite atomic dual records from \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\).  Their rational weights and rational real-algebraic support encodings make membership in finite unions \(D_v\), and the finitely many quadratic distance tests defining \(H_r\), decidable by exact sign computation.  Refining the Gaussian enclosures gives a rational lower endpoint \(l^-_{\nu,s}\) for each feasible dual objective.  Put
\[
L_s=\max_{\nu\text{ processed by }s}l^-_{\nu,s},
\qquad
U_s=\min_{Q\text{ accepted by }s}U_{Q,s},                                    \tag{38}
\]
leaving an endpoint undefined while its finite collection is empty.  Weak duality and (37) imply
\[
L_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\leq U_s                                      \tag{39}
\]
whenever both endpoints are defined.

Every fixed stage terminates: it contains finitely many rational linear programs and exact sign tests.  Each requested Gaussian enclosure integrates on a rational box using the certified compact modulus carried by the finite record and bounds the complement by its certified Gaussian tail.  Subdivision width and tail mass tend to zero, so every positive requested enclosure width is reached after finitely many operations.

By attainment, choose \(K^*\in\mathcal C_\eta\) with \(R_r(K^*)=M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  For any rational \(\zeta>0\), sufficiently fine evaluation of the record from (33) yields
\[
c^-_{Q_j(K^*),s}\geq c\{Q_j(K^*)\}-\zeta,
\qquad
r^+_{Q_j(K^*),s}\leq r\{Q_j(K^*)\}+\zeta.                                  \tag{40}
\]
Thus \(\rho_{Q_j(K^*),s}\leq\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\), and (33), (35), (37), and one further outward width \(\zeta\) give
\[
U_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+2\zeta
+\frac{D\{\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\}}
{\eta+\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta}.                                      \tag{41}
\]
The denominator is positive because \(\eta>0\).  First increase \(j\), then decrease \(\zeta\), to make the excess in (41) vanish.  The atomic-density conclusion of \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\) and refinement of lower enclosures give \(L_s\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  Together with (39)--(41), some finite stage satisfies \(U_s-L_s\leq\varepsilon\).

For the complexity receipt, let \(a_i(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the number of stage-\(s\) operations of type \(i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\}\), and let \(b(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the largest integer bit length occurring at that stage.  These are computable because the stage is finite.  Define by primitive recursion
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_i(0)&=a_i(\mathfrak G,0),&
C_i(s+1)&=C_i(s)+a_i(\mathfrak G,s+1),\\
B_*(0)&=b(\mathfrak G,0),&
B_*(s+1)&=\max\{B_*(s),b(\mathfrak G,s+1)\}.
\end{aligned}                                                                  \tag{42}
\]
Let
\[
s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)
=\min\{s:L_s,U_s\text{ are defined and }U_s-L_s\leq\varepsilon\}.           \tag{43}
\]
The test is rational, and the preceding convergence proves that its sequential search halts.  Hence \(s_*\) is total recursive under the conditional premise.  The advertised functions are
\[
N_i(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=C_i\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\},
\qquad
\operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=B_*\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\}. \tag{44}
\]
Archiving the repaired primal attaining the finite minimum and the atomic dual attaining the finite maximum in (38) gives the replayable certificate.  Equations (39), (43), and (44) prove the endpoints, gap, termination, and five-part receipt.  The proof used (33) as a premise and therefore does not answer the open-ended question.

\textbf{Technique: composition of finite-fiber identification, exact tangent geometry, compact experiment comparison, and a restricted comparator embedding.}

Let \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) and \(p_0=p(P_0)\).  The separate restrictions in \(\text{def:causal-model}\) include \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\geq m_*>0\), so every conditional quantile in the causal target has positive denominator.  By \(\text{thm:causal-label-polyhedralization}\), the observed-cell contrasts identify the selected-complier submeasures and the response-type fiber is exactly the compatible full-law fiber.  By \(\text{prop:lower-endpoint-attainment}\) and \(\text{prop:upper-endpoint-attainment}\), for every fixed \(t\in\mathcal T\),
\[
\begin{split}
Q_{1,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)&=\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\\
Q_{1,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)&=\overline\Delta(t;p_0).
\end{split}                                                                    \tag{49}
\]
For any single \(P\in\mathcal F(p_0)\), the definitions of infimum and supremum give
\[
\underline\Delta(t;p_0)
\leq Q_{1,P}(t)-Q_{0,P}(t)
\leq\overline\Delta(t;p_0).                                                    \tag{50}
\]
Taking all coordinates and then all compatible laws in (50) proves the displayed outer bound.  The witnesses in (49) may depend on \(t\) and on the chosen endpoint, so the argument proves no rectangle equality.

Under relative interiority and tangent-image compatibility, \(\text{prop:tangent-fan-global-cover}\) gives \(\bigcup_vD_v^0=\mathbb R^d\).  Full column rank of \(B\) and positive coordinates of \(p_0\) imply, for \(x\ne0\),
\[
x'I_0x=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\frac{\{(Bx)_j\}^2}{(p_0)_j}>0.                 \tag{51}
\]
Thus \(I_0\succ0\) and \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\); rational \(p_0\) and \(B\) make \(\Sigma_0\) rational.  Proposition \(\text{prop:job-corps-radius-nonempty}\) supplies \(H_{r_0}\ne\varnothing\).  These cover, covariance, rational-cell, and separated-domain facts are exactly the membership conditions of \(\mathfrak E\), hence \(\mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E\).

The proof of \(\text{thm:fixed-stratum-transfer}\) gives the compact error
\[
C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
+(H_C+A_0)\{d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)\}
+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C),                                             \tag{52}
\]
without calling the full expression \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  The unconditional \(\text{lem:moving-offset-carter-geometry}\) and \(\text{thm:moving-offset-transfer}\) give qualitative moving-offset comparison for every supplied Gaussian rule.  Their proofs show separately that effective compatible density is used only to construct a finite Gaussian rule, while effective rational envelopes for the statistical terms are additionally required for replayable sampled-data accounting.

Under zero-offset centering, \(\text{thm:compact-exhaustion-transfer}\) gives
\[
M_n^\diamond\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
\qquad
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n\geq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).                  \tag{53}
\]
Its proof selects the windows diagonally by eventual compact inequalities; it does not compute convergence indices.  If effective compatible density is affirmatively resolved, \(\text{thm:certglue-termination}\) gives the finite Gaussian primal, atomic dual, outward endpoints, and cost receipt.  The additional envelopes stated in the moving theorem are precisely what makes its sampled-data transfer replayable.  Lemma \(\text{lem:escaping-boundary-kill}\) excludes a global upper conclusion from compact-uniform comparison, proving all negative scope clauses in the statement.

Finally, \(\text{prop:bffl-discrete-perfect-compliance-embedding}\) checks the Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes comparison only after imposing singleton \(X\), known positive rational assignment, perfect compliance, positive-direction employment monotonicity, finite wage support, and positive always-employed mass.  Its equations (45)--(48) identify \(ASC=EE\) and \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\).  Because those restrictions are not properties of the unrestricted comparator class, and because marginal witnesses need not be one joint witness, no broader inclusion or sharpness transfer follows.

Assume multinomial interiority, base convergence, compact-uniform centered local expansion, the local-family affine-hull condition, and the completed moving-slack construction.  Fix a rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\).  Choose \(\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\cap\mathbb Q^{|\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}|}\) with \(\|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\leq\xi_n\), and define
\[
 d_n(C)=\sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}-Bu\right\|_2,
 \qquad
 \delta_n(C)=\max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|,
\]
with the maximum equal to zero when the active list is empty.  Put
\[
\chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n,
\qquad
A_0=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}.
\]
For any supplied nonnegative upper bound \(\overline\chi_n(C)\geq\chi_n(C)\), and any supplied Gaussian rule on the \(\widehat c_n\)-offset experiment, the parameter-independent Carter and score transfer produces a multinomial rule whose semantic coverage deficit and normalized separated-risk excess on \(C\) are each no larger than the corresponding supplied Gaussian quantity plus
\[
\Delta_n(C)=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
+(H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C).                                                  \tag{11}
\]
The assertion is unconditional on effective compatible density and does not assert that \(\overline\chi_n(C)\) is effectively available.  If \(\overline\chi_n(C)\to0\), then \(\Delta_n(C)\to0\).

In the randomized-treatment model of Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes, Assumption A requires random treatment assignment, Assumption B requires \(S(1)\geq S(0)\) unit by unit, the always-employed stratum is \(EE=\{S(0)=S(1)=1\}\), and Proposition 1 gives lower and upper quantile-treatment-effect bounds for that stratum under Assumptions A--B.

Consider the singleton-covariate submodel \(\mathcal X=\{x_0\}\) with known rational assignment probabilities \(\bar\pi_z\geq\pi_*\), perfect compliance \(D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=z\), \(s(x_0)=+1\), finite-grid potential wages \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)\in\mathcal Y\), observed variables generated by the declared consistency maps, randomized assignment, monotone employment \(S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)\geq S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\), and \(P(EE)\geq m_*>0\), where \(EE=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\).  The induced law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\); every unit is a complier, the always-selected-complier event equals \(EE\), and
\[
M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE).
\]
This is an embedding only of that discrete perfect-compliance submodel. added_lemmas.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: direct verification of every maintained restriction and equality of principal strata.}

The cited node \(\text{lem:bffl-randomized-always-employed-model}\) records the source model's randomization, employment monotonicity, and always-employed target.  We verify only the stated restricted embedding.  Since \(\mathcal X=\{x_0\}\), \(P(X=x_0)=1\geq\pi_*\).  The declared table has \(\pi_z(x_0)=\bar\pi_z\geq\pi_*\), so the known-assignment and instrument-stratum positivity conditions hold.  Random assignment gives the conditional independence condition because conditioning on the constant \(X\) changes nothing.

Perfect compliance gives, for every unit,
\[
D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1>0=D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0).                                  \tag{45}
\]
Thus the no-defiers restriction holds and every unit is a complier.  Defining \(D=D^{\mathrm{pot}}(Z)\), \(S=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(D)\), and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(D)\) on \(\{S=1\}\), with \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=\dagger\) on \(\{S=0\}\), verifies the three consistency and exclusion conditions equation by equation.  Because \(s(x_0)=+1\), employment monotonicity gives
\[
s(x_0)\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)-S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\}
=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)-S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\geq0,                               \tag{46}
\]
so the complier-conditional selection-monotonicity condition holds.  The finite wage-grid premise gives the declared outcome support.

By (45), the always-selected-complier event is
\[
\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),
S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}=EE.                              \tag{47}
\]
Random assignment, perfect compliance, and the consistency maps reduce the observed contrasts defining \(c_{axk}\) to
\[
c_{0x_0k}=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1,Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=y_k\},
\qquad
c_{1x_0k}=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1,Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=y_k\}.                 \tag{47a}
\]
Indeed, in each arm the compatible treatment cell has probability \(\bar\pi_z\) times the displayed potential-outcome event, while the cross-treatment cell is empty by perfect compliance; division is valid because \(\bar\pi_z\geq\pi_*>0\).  Summing (47a) over the finite wage grid gives
\[
q_{0x_0}=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\},
\qquad
q_{1x_0}=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}.                                         \tag{47b}
\]
Monotone employment implies that the first event is contained in the second.  Consequently
\[
m_{x_0}=\min\{q_{0x_0},q_{1x_0}\}
=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\}=P(EE).                                           \tag{47c}
\]
There is one covariate cell, so summing (47c) over the singleton support gives
\[
M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\geq m_*>0.                                             \tag{48}
\]
All nine restrictions in \(\text{def:causal-model}\) have now been checked, proving membership in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  Perfect compliance and the singleton support are extra restrictions, so this argument proves only a submodel embedding.  Removing either does not follow from Assumptions A--B or Proposition 1, and nothing in the cited marginal bound constructs a common latent completion for several quantiles; therefore neither unrestricted-class inclusion nor same-law joint sharpness follows.
